rulings.Calendar Matter: Renewed Motion To Seal Materials Filed With Stipulation And [Proposed] Order For Filing Of [Proposed] Amended Cross-Complaint
rulings.Rulings: Matter on the LAW AND MOTION / DISCOVERY Calendar for Monday, Sep-14-2026. LINE 10. PLAINTIFF X CORP.'s Renewed Motion To Seal Materials Filed With Stipulation And [Proposed] Order For Filing Of [Proposed] Amended Cross-Complaint. Plaintiff X Corp.'s renewed motion to seal materials filed with stipulation for filing of proposed amended cross-complaint is denied. While there is an improved showing from the prior motion, X Corp. still fails to provide facts, rather than conclusions to support its assertions that the materials sought to be sealed are confidential and commercially sensitive business information and there is a substantial probability that its claimed overriding interest would be prejudiced if this motion is denied. For instance, there is no showing that there is any contractual or other restriction requiring defendant Erik McAfee to keep the materials confidential or that competitors of X Corp. are unable to find out this information from Mr. McAfee or others. Disputes over stock options and other items of compensation are commonplace involving companies with competitors and routinely the public is not prevented from learning the specifics of the stock options and compensation at issue. X Corp. fails to present facts to show that its materials should be treated differently and in derogation of the public's strong right of access to information that is material to the resolution of litigated cases in the courts. rulings.Case Title: KIMBERLY MAYS VS. SUTTER HEALTH - SUTTER BAY HOSPITALS, DBA ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: DEMURRER to Amended COMPLAINT
rulings.Rulings: Matter on the LAW AND MOTION / DISCOVERY Calendar for Monday, Sep-14-2026. LINE 12. DEFENDANT ACTALENT SCIENTIFIC LLC's DEMURRER to 2ND Amended COMPLAINT. Defendant Actalent Scientific LLC's demurrer to all three causes of action alleged against it in the second amended complaint filed by plaintiff Kimberly Mays is sustained without leave to amend, but the court re-affirms the prior order granting Mays leave to allege a general negligence claim against Actalent. Mays' hostile work environment and failure to prevent claims fail to allege ultimate facts for the required showing that Actalent knew or should have known of the alleged harassing conduct. Mays' allegations in paragraphs 50-52 of her second amended complaint are conclusions, not ultimate facts. There is nothing in those paragraphs from which it can be reasonably inferred that Actalent should have known about Fifer's alleged harassing conduct. Mays' constructive discharge claim fails to allege ultimate facts for the required showing that Actalent intentionally created or knowingly permitted the alleged intolerable conditions that resulted in Mays' resignation. Mays' allegations in paragraph 104 of her second amended complaint are conclusions, not ultimate facts. Because Mays has not stated or suggested that she is aware of any additional facts that she is able to allege that support these claims, Mays has not shown that there is a reasonable possibility that she is able to remediate the deficiencies in these claims and thus her request for leave to amend is denied as to these claims. However, although given leave to do so in the order filed April 16, 2026 May did not allege a general negligence claim against Actalent in her second amended complaint. Her request that she be allowed to do so in a further amended complaint is granted. For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 301 remotely or in person. rulings.Case Title: ROBERT STEWART VS. ERICA PYCH KURIEN D.O.
rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion And Motion To Strike Plaintiff?S First Amended Complaint
rulings.Rulings: Matter on the LAW AND MOTION / DISCOVERY Calendar for Monday, Sep-14-2026. LINE 14. DEFENDANT ERICA KURIEN's Motion To Strike Plaintiff's First Amended Complaint. Defendant Erica Kurien's motion to strike plaintiff Robert Stewart's first amended complaint is denied. This motion places form over substance. While Kurien is correct that Stewart was required to seek leave of court to file his first amended complaint, Kurien fails to identify any reason why, had Stewart done so, leave would have been denied. The strong policy of California is to liberally allow amendment of pleadings. In the court's discretion and in the interests of judicial economy, Stewart's opposition papers are treated as a motion for leave and, as so treated, the motion is granted. Defendant The Regents of the University of California's motion for terminating sanctions is denied. Although the motion is unopposed, the Regents have not shown that there is no less restrictive alternative to the drastic and extraordinary relief that they seek, especially considering that the trial date is not for more than nineteen months and this case appears not to involve any novel or complex issues.
